author: China Insights
description:
A Chinese Long March 7A rocket exploded just 85 seconds after launch on August 10, after completing 16 consecutive successful missions.

The failure came at a particularly sensitive moment. Just weeks earlier, former Politburo member Ma Xingrui—one of the most prominent political figures to emerge from China’s aerospace establishment—had been expelled from the Communist Party.

Why did a mature rocket suddenly fail? Why was China pushing to break its launch-interval record? And what does the accident reveal about the dramatic purge of China’s aerospace and military-industrial elite?

In this episode, we examine:

• Why the 85-second failure is technically significant
• What Max-Q means for a rocket during launch
• Why China’s push for shorter launch intervals raises questions
• The strategic importance of the Zhongxing-4 satellite mission
• The potential implications for the YF-100 engine family
• How China’s aerospace establishment became a political talent pipeline
• The rise and fa
title: China’s “Golden Rocket” Explodes After 16 Straight Launches — What Went Wrong? I China Insights
